characteristics.cultivar: Local Anhua tea bushes, select tender young leaf material

description.short: Loose-leaf top-grade dark tea made from tender spring leaves — historically an elite Anhua specialty, gentler than compressed bricks
description.overview: Unlike Fu Zhuan and other compressed bricks from Anhua, Tian Jian was historically preserved in loose-leaf form and reserved for affluent patrons and local gentry rather than long-distance caravan transport.
description.leaf: Loose, dark, twisted leaves made from select tender spring pluckings
description.liquor: Deep amber, clearer and brighter than heavily compressed dark teas
description.aroma: Mellow and earthy, with subtle sweetness
description.taste: Soft, smooth, and refined, much less astringent and coarse than brick dark teas from the same region
description.processing: Harvesting select tender young leaves → kill-green → rolling → post-fermentation piling without heavy brick compression, keeping the leaves loose

history.origin: The historical grading system of Anhua dark tea divided harvests into three 'Jian' tiers, where 'Tian Jian' ('Heavenly Tip') represented the highest loose-leaf grade, separate from raw material destined for brick compression.
history.development: While compressed categories (like Fu Zhuan) were designed for rough overland export to border nomadic peoples, Tian Jian remained a luxury tribute and domestic premium tea.
history.modern: Today it is one of the most highly prized loose dark teas of Hunan, cherished as an elegant, nuanced alternative to compressed Hei Cha.
interestingFacts: The name 'Heavenly Tip' signifies the supreme grade in the traditional three-tier Jian hierarchy (Tian Jian, Sheng Jian, and Gong Jian).
Unlike the vast majority of dark teas synonymous with tightly compressed bricks and cakes, Tian Jian is a rare example of a high-grade loose-leaf Hei Cha.
